summary: This is a request for a right total knee arthroplasty (CPT 27447) for primary osteoarthritis in a 67-year-old male. Criteria C1 (KL grade 4 on X-ray), C3 (functional limitation), C4 (BMI 34.1) and C5 (no signs of infection) are met. C2 is not met: documented conservative treatment began 08/20/2026, about 8 weeks before the 10/15/2026 consult, so the reviewer may want to ask whether any earlier nonsurgical treatment was given during the 3-year pain history.

criteria.text: Radiographic evidence of advanced osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4) of the affected knee.

evidence.quote: Severe medial joint-space narrowing with bone-on-bone contact.

criteria.rationale: The right knee X-ray report documents Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 with bone-on-bone contact.

criteria.text: At least 12 weeks of documented nonsurgical treatment (physical therapy, NSAIDs, injections, bracing or weight loss).

evidence.quote: Started physical therapy on 08/20/2026 and completed 6 weeks.
One corticosteroid injection on 09/12/2026 with 2 weeks of relief.

criteria.rationale: The earliest documented nonsurgical treatment began 08/20/2026. From then to the 10/15/2026 note is 56 days, about 8 weeks. That is short of the required 12 weeks. No earlier conservative treatment is documented, even though pain is reported for 3 years.

criteria.text: Pain or functional limitation that interferes with activities of daily living.

evidence.quote: can no longer walk more than 2 blocks or kneel at church.

criteria.rationale: The note documents limits on walking distance, stairs, standing and kneeling, which interfere with daily activities.

criteria.text: BMI below 40, or documented medical optimization if BMI is 40 or above.
criteria.rationale: The most recent BMI is 34.1, which is below 40.

criteria.text: No active infection in or around the knee.

evidence.quote: No erythema, warmth or effusion. Skin intact. No history of joint infection.

criteria.rationale: The exam shows no signs of infection, the skin is intact, and there is no history of joint infection. Fever is not explicitly addressed.
